title: Quartz Programme
body_html:
Summary

Automate the functional verification of the CARESCAPE Central Station (Meridian) so that regulated, evidence-backed six-month cyber releases no longer depend on slow, manual testing.

Details

Client area: Acme Health, Clinical Systems
Our firm: Northwind
Status: the solution design (v1.1, 21 July 2026) is awaiting formal sign-off before full-scale development.

Why it exists

Meridian functional verification is manual, repetitive and error prone: 329 verification procedures with 2,711 steps across 6 SVP and 1 DVP documents, with results compared and screenshots captured by hand. Because the Meridian is a regulated medical device, gaps in the evidence can invalidate a run.

Approach in plain words

  • Robot Framework and Python libraries drive the application and produce the evidence.
  • Dual-driver approach: WinAppDriver and the Java Access Bridge (accessibility tree) for the MFC and Java parts of the UI; computer vision (OpenCV, Tesseract OCR, a trained YOLO model) for complex UI checks.
  • Black-box: attaches to the running application, no source code or changes to the device.
  • Each run produces one consolidated HTML report and a regulatory-format PDF with timestamped screenshots.

Delivery plan (proposal v2)

Hybrid strategy: about 70% manual and 30% selective automation, 24 weeks, fixed-scope and milestone-based.

PhaseFocus
1 Discovery and requirements sign-offRequirements, architecture, environment planning
2 Platform foundationDrivers and vision AI
3 Test suite authoringTest suites in Robot Framework, per component
4 Code quality and stabilisationReview, refactor, self-healing, final regression
5 Sign-off, knowledge transfer and go-liveUAT, handover, 90-day hypercare

Success targets (proposal v2)

  • Driver coverage of 95% or more of identified UI elements
  • YOLO detection precision 95% or more, recall 90% or more
  • Automated suite 98% or more stable over three consecutive runs
  • 100% of in-scope scenarios traceable from requirement to result
  • End state: Acme Health team runs the suite independently

Open points

  • The proposal and the solution design count scope differently (about 2,500 to 3,000 scenarios versus 329 procedures). TODO: confirm the agreed scope.
  • Solution design approvers: Emerson Marsh (executive), Remy Finch (technical), Udayashankar Jinde (program), B.S Ganesha (architecture). All pending.

Showcase

A medical technology company verified a regulated medical device application by hand: 329 verification procedures with 2,711 steps, results compared and screenshots captured manually. Gaps in the evidence could invalidate a whole run.

Northwind is automating the verification with Robot Framework and Python. The suite drives the application as a black box, with no access to its source code, through the Windows UI automation and Java accessibility layers, and uses computer vision (OpenCV, OCR and a trained YOLO model) for complex screens. Each run produces one consolidated HTML report and a regulatory-format PDF with timestamped screenshots.

Targets: 95% or more coverage of the user interface, a suite that is 98% or more stable over three consecutive runs, full traceability from requirement to result, and the client's own team running the suite independently.

Source documents

  • Relay Design
  • Orbit Proposal (contains commercial terms; internal only)
